$comment: Deployment facts — the single machine-readable registry of deployment truth for ApexMail. External audit 2026-10-02 item #14: every claim surface (marketing, compliance templates, compare pages, docs prose) and both evidence gates (tools/check_capability_claims.py, tools/check_security_posture.py) consume THIS file as the shared authority, so two surfaces can never disagree about the same fact again. Every fact is DERIVED FROM the authoritative sources only — docs/operations/disaster-recovery.md (canonical DR), ci/README.md (supply chain), docker-compose.yml + docker-compose.prod.yml + .env.production.example (runtime), docs/development/capability-registry.json (implementation stages), deploy/ (monitoring reality) — never from marketing or compliance prose. When one of those sources changes, update the fact here IN THE SAME CHANGE; the checkers fail on drift.
$schema_comment: Every entry in `facts` carries the audit schema: `value` (the fact itself), plus six per-audit-2026-10-02 fields — `implementation_stage` (ladder stage from docs/development/capability-registry.json: implemented | integration-tested | runtime-wired | deployed | monitored | advertised; 'absent' when nothing exists in the tree), `binary_default` (what the code/compose does absent an explicit operator decision), `managed_cloud_enabled` (whether the managed production baseline — .env.production.example + docker-compose.prod.yml — turns it ON), `enforcement_mode` (enforced | detection-only/tag | flag | monitor | not-applicable), `monitored` (an alert rule or dashboard in deploy/ covers it), `advertised` (a customer-facing surface claims it as active) — plus `evidence` (where the truth lives in the tree) and `source` (the authoritative document that owns the fact).

deployment.host: one Hetzner host (Finland), full stack under Docker Compose
deployment.orchestration: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml (+ the generated per-run docker-compose.digest-override.yml from the release manifest)
deployment.canonical_deploy_invocation: ci/pipeline.sh run (host timer) — deploy/scripts/deploy.sh is the manual fallback; a bare `docker compose up` without the digest override is unsupported for production
deployment.failover: none — host failure is an outage until the host is rebuilt; recovery = host rebuild + backup restore

topology.evidence: docker-compose.prod.yml (one host, all services); docs/operations/disaster-recovery.md reality table

postgres_pitr.evidence: no archive_command / WAL-archive service in docker-compose*.yml; docs/operations/disaster-recovery.md: 'WAL archiving / PITR — Not implemented. Recovery point granularity is the last nightly backup (RPO up to ~24 h)'

wal_archiving.evidence: docs/operations/disaster-recovery.md reality table; no archive_command in any compose file

standby_regions.evidence: docs/operations/disaster-recovery.md: 'Standby region — None. There is no second region, no replication, no region failover'

artifact_digest_pin.binary_default: base compose carries logical :latest tags BY DESIGN; the canonical deploy ALWAYS layers the generated digest override
artifact_digest_pin.enforcement_mode: enforced (ci/stages/deploy.sh refuses to bring up services whose live image digest differs from the release manifest; tools/check_image_pinning.py gates the rendered config)
artifact_digest_pin.evidence: ci/stages/images.sh renders release-manifest.json + docker-compose.digest-override.yml per run (SHA256SUMS.images); ci/stages/deploy.sh applies the override and re-verifies digests; deploy/scripts/deploy.sh renders the same pair for the manual path

artifact_signature.evidence: ci/README.md §5: 'GHCR push + image provenance/SBOM attestation signatures — dropped (no registry by design)'; no cosign/provenance attestation anywhere in ci/

sbom.binary_default: Trivy SPDX JSON per image, written into the CI run dir
sbom.enforcement_mode: advisory (SBOM generation warns on failure; the separate Trivy vuln gate is blocking)
sbom.evidence: ci/stages/security.sh _trivy_sbom (spdx-json into $RUN_DIR) + ci/stages/images.sh sbom_digest in release-manifest.json; nothing signs the SBOM

image_signing.evidence: SHA256SUMS.images is a digest INTEGRITY manifest, not a signature; no signing key/cosign in ci/

dependabot.evidence: ci/README.md §5: 'Dependabot + auto-merge — gone | manual cargo update → check-pr.sh full → push'; .github/dependabot.yml is vestigial (its own comments say so; auto-merge is archived) and must not be claimed as a control

firewall_inbound_ports.enforcement_mode: enforced (UFW default-deny incoming; only these service ports plus the operator set below are allowed)
firewall_inbound_ports.evidence: deploy/scripts/hetzner-bootstrap.sh configure_ufw (allow 22, 80, 443, 25, 587, 465, 993, 2525, 2526); the customer-facing service subset is 25/80/443/587/993 (SMTP, HTTP/S, submission, IMAP)

firewall_inbound_ports_operator.enforcement_mode: enforced (22 = SSH key-only admin; 465 = SMTPS; 2525/2526 = bounce/FBL feeds)

fim_inotify.evidence: no file-integrity monitoring daemon (no AIDE/inotify watcher) in deploy/ or compose; the only file-watcher is the TLS-renewal restart path unit (deploy/hardening/apexmail-tls-renew-restart.path), which restarts containers — it is not FIM

deployment_log_append_only.binary_default: every CI run writes ci/runs/<ts>/manifest.json (stage name/status/exit_code/duration) — records exist but the store is ordinary files, pruned to the newest CI_KEEP_RUNS
deployment_log_append_only.evidence: ci/README.md §1 (run manifest + pruning to newest 30 runs); NOT a tamper-evident, append-only customer-facing ledger

postgres_page_checksums.evidence: postgres runs without --data-checksums (no checksum init in docker-compose.yml / prod bootstrap); no nightly full-scan job exists. The REAL integrity control is the audit-log hash chain (chained SHA-256, crates/compliance + worker graduation writer)

backup_restore_automatic.binary_default: automated portion = decrypt + pg_restore --list (structure validation) after every backup, before the plaintext is deleted; FULL restore drills are MANUAL at the documented quarterly cadence
backup_restore_automatic.enforcement_mode: enforced (a backup that cannot be decrypted and read is never counted as good)
backup_restore_automatic.evidence: deploy/hardening/scripts/postgres-backup-encrypt.sh (verify-restorability step); backup container healthchecks (artifact newer than 25 h) in docker-compose.prod.yml; drills: docs/operations/disaster-recovery-testing.md (quarterly)

data_loss_prevention.enforcement_mode: enforced (worker pre-send gate: medium-severity findings quarantine/defer the send, high severity refuse it; engine errors fail OPEN, detections fail CLOSED)
data_loss_prevention.evidence: WORKER_DLP_ENABLED=true in .env.production.example (managed baseline, compose ${VAR:?}-guarded); wired in worker-processors email/processor.rs + email/dlp.rs; the managed cloud advertises outbound DLP (compliance templates), the marketing security page does not name it

web_application_firewall.enforcement_mode: enforced (managed baseline pins WAF_ENFORCE=true; would-block verdicts block)
web_application_firewall.evidence: WAF_ENABLED=true + WAF_ENFORCE=true in .env.production.example (compose ${VAR:?}-guarded); api-server app.rs waf middleware mount

spam_phishing_filtering.enforcement_mode: detection-only/tag (MTA_SPAM_FILTER_ENABLED=true; REJECT-classified refusal is a separate explicit opt-in, MTA_SPAM_REJECT_ENABLED=false)

intrusion_detection_prevention.enforcement_mode: detection-only/tag (MTA_IDS_ENABLED=true; MTA_IDS_REFUSE=false, refusal is a separate explicit opt-in)

attachment_sandboxing.enforcement_mode: flag (MTA_ATTACHMENT_SCAN_MODE=flag — static + content inspection tags mail; strip/reject are explicit operator modes)

arc_sealing.gate: SMTP_ARC_SEAL env / mta config arc_seal — config-gated, binary default FALSE; the production compose and the managed baseline do NOT set it, so the managed cloud does not seal
arc_sealing.evidence: services/mail-server/crates/mta/src/config.rs (arc_seal: parse_bool_env("SMTP_ARC_SEAL", false); servers/inbound.rs seals only when config.arc_seal); SMTP_ARC_SEAL absent from docker-compose*.yml and .env.production.example

bimi_delivery_verification.evidence: crates/mta/src/auth/bimi.rs verify_bimi is not consumed by the mail flow; the email grader performs an advisory BIMI DNS record CHECK only — not logo verification in delivery

mta_sts_enforcement.evidence: crates/mta/src/auth/mta_sts.rs has no server-path consumer; no MTA-STS policy file or TLSRPT stream under deploy/ — neither policy publication nor outbound enforcement is part of the running topology

dane_tlsa_verification.evidence: crates/mta/src/auth/dane.rs consumers are limited to the crates/mta/src/auth re-exports; neither the inbound nor the outbound delivery path verifies DANE/TLSA

branch_protection_codeowners.evidence: CODEOWNERS-based review enforcement is NOT yet proven: scripts/verify-branch-protection.sh (audit item #13) queries the live GitHub branch-protection API and fails closed, but no recorded PASS exists, so the fact stays operator-pending. Real gates that DO run today (ci/README.md §4): pre-push hook, ci/check-pr.sh, and the deploy-host pipeline that stops the line before images/deploy; branch protection on main requires the 'woodpecker' commit-status context (ci/README.md §12). Do NOT claim codeowner review until scripts/verify-branch-protection.sh returns PASS and this fact is flipped

ai_reply_classification.enforcement_mode: advisory classification (semantic layer 2 of deterministic -> AI -> policy); ANY failure (outage, disabled model, invalid output) falls back to Unknown/0.0 — never a guessed disposition
ai_reply_classification.evidence: WORKER_REPLY_CLASSIFIER_AI_ENABLED=true (+ WORKER_REPLY_CLASSIFIER_AI_URL) in .env.production.example and docker-compose.yml (worker service); the route is POST /reply/classify on ai-service (crates/ai-service/src/reply_classify.rs, service-token domain, tenant-header rate governor); the client is crates/worker-processors/src/reply_handler/ai.rs (HttpReplyClassifier); the wire contract is pinned cross-crate by crates/integration-tests/tests/reply_classify_contract_tests.rs

inbound_reply_mirroring.evidence: crates/mta/src/servers/inbound.rs parse_inbound_mirrors (from_email/to_email/message_id_header/subject/body_text/body_html/headers populated in the accept-time INSERT; NUL-sanitised, best-effort — a parse failure never rejects mail); the reply handler's claim predicate is inbound_messages.from_email IS NOT NULL (crates/worker-processors/src/reply_handler/processor.rs)

mta_event_webhooks.evidence: crates/mta/src/servers/util.rs queue_tenant_webhook_event fans message.inbound (inbound.rs), message.bounced (bounce.rs) and message.complained (feedback_loop.rs) into the canonical webhook_queue table the worker's webhook processor drains (retries, circuit breaker, SSRF guard); docs/api/webhooks.md documents message.inbound; the former mta:webhook_queue Redis list is deleted (no consumer ever existed)

email_draft_agent.enforcement_mode: draft-only (every reply is stored pending_approval=true for human review; the agent refuses to start when AI_EMAIL_REQUIRE_APPROVAL is not set)
email_draft_agent.evidence: ai-service bin/server.rs spawns EmailAnswerer over the process pool/LLM/governor when AI_EMAIL_AGENT_ENABLED=true (crates/ai-service/src/email_agent.rs); compose + .env.production.example set the managed baseline ON with AI_REPLY_FROM and the poll cadence; drafts are grounded against knowledge::shared_knowledge_markdown() via verifier::verify_grounded and reviewed through /v1/admin/ai/drafts

console_assistant.evidence: console page /assistant (crates/ui-foundation leptos_views::web_assistant_page + the SSR manifest route), server-side sessions in migration 240_ai_chat_sessions.sql, PRG handler crates/api-server/src/routes/web.rs::form_assistant_message over the shared proxy crates/api-server/src/routes/ai_chat.rs::session_turn_inner (4,000-char cap, per-user Redis limiter, tenant-scoped account context); per-tenant feature flag ai_chat

objection_handling.enforcement_mode: advisory (drafts are generated only from an owner/counsel-approved, in-window library entry plus the canonical facts; every draft still requires human approval)
objection_handling.evidence: migration 242_objection_library.sql (taxonomy CHECK + the evidence gate: an external-copy-eligible entry without evidence is refused by the schema); ai-service crates/ai-service/src/reply_classify.rs emits/validates the sub-label (OBJECTION_CLASSES); the worker parses it (crates/worker-processors/src/reply_handler/ai.rs) and persists it on the classification row (sales_reply_classifications.objection_class); the mailbot loads the approved entry (crates/ai-service/src/email_agent.rs::load_objection_guidance) into the prompt and the grounding sources, so guidance text is grounded while anything else still needs canonical facts
